claims.text: A small volume fraction of MoS2 nanoplatelets can be uniformly dispersed within a high-entropy-alloy matrix during processing.
Dispersed MoS2 nanoplatelets migrate or concentrate at the contact surface during sliding.
MoS2 nanoplatelets form an in situ lubricious surface tribolayer during sliding.
The resulting tribolayer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
MoS2 shears easily and produces a low-shear-strength tribolayer.
The low-shear-strength tribolayer reduces the coefficient of friction.
The MoS2-derived tribolayer protects the high-entropy-alloy substrate from wear.
MoS2 has sufficient inherent thermal stability to maintain its lubricating performance over a wide service-temperature range.
Adding MoS2 nanoplatelets will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 20% relative to the untreated alloy.
Adding MoS2 nanoplatelets will reduce the wear rate by approximately 30% relative to the untreated alloy.
The predicted reductions in friction and wear will occur across multiple operating temperatures, from room temperature to elevated service temperatures.
The beneficial effects require the solid-lubricant phase to remain uniformly dispersed and retained at the sliding interface.
Preserved interfacial bonding during thermal cycling is required for continued effectiveness.
Excessive additive content may weaken the structural integrity of the alloy.
Poor additive dispersion may prevent effective tribofilm formation.
